svg.title: Copper Scroll entry 17: the two domes(?) in the Valley of Achor
svg.text: Entry 17 (IV 6–8) — the two domes(?) in the Valley of Achor
Schematic plan, north up. One arrangement the text allows; the pair's spacing and the side of the valley are not given.
Project reading: two domes(?) or cavities, the deposit midway
Project text הכיפין “domes(?)”; Puech reads הכינין “the two cavities”.
Midway is taken between the two openings; their spacing is not given.
rock of the valley side (side not given)
engraved עכון; all editions read Achor
spacing between the pair: not given
Midpoint between the openings; chamber-centre or path midpoints are other models.
Wadi Nuweiʿimeh cliffs: Eisenberg's pair, north up. Dots, not plans.
≈ 71 m apart by the printed grid (0–141 m); V/38 and V/28–29
lie between; path route not described; no midpoint drawn.
Milik 1962 (DJD D5 p. 263): trees that “could easily have
disappeared”; nothing would be left to find.
Lefkovits 2000 pp. 162–164. In the Buqeia, Iron Age ruins
could serve, but nothing selects a pair (phase 5).
the landmark word is read with kaf, bet or taw; the
project text's הכיפין matches none of the three forms
a pair, the deposit midway, 3 cubits down, two pots of
engraved עכון, Achor in every edition; Wadi Nuweiʿimeh
or the Buqeia is placement only.
“Between the two domes(?) that are in the Valley of Achor, midway between them, dig three cubits:
there are two pots full of silver.”
Two hollow features in the valley, as Puech's cavities. Their spacing and the valley side are
arbitrary. Midway is between the openings; three cubits is a depth.
Atlas: best-supported, medium. Wadi Nuweiʿimeh NE of Jericho preferred (medium); the Buqeia plateau
possible (medium); the ʿAin Duk springs possible (low).
Caves by the Naʿima valley were in use 1st c. BCE–1st c. CE, but no source reports a pair
(phase5_assessments.csv). V/49 + V/48: spacing ~71 m, no midpoint (feature_constraints.csv).
